originality.rationale: The general g-minimal concept and pair-hull characterization are prior work (Brown–Oellermann 2014). The assessed claim is the exact uniform sharp bound on opposite-side missing degrees versus both side sizes, the boundary family for every parameter and the online/statistical dimensions. Actual targeted published-finding corpus and primary-literature searches found no proven domination. Full texts of the two most plausible published sources remained inaccessible, a material priority caveat; accessible abstracts do not assert a sharp 2t+3 threshold.
residual_risks: Brown–Oellermann 2014 full article unavailable: a specific extremal density corollary could exist beyond its abstract.
Thiessen–Gärtner ECML PKDD 2022 article full text unavailable: specialized examples or online bounds could cover the learning dimensions.
Unindexed equivalent nomenclature or unsearched monographs could contain the quantitative threshold.

value.rationale: The sharp robust threshold for arbitrary near-complete bipartite graphs is a natural extremal invariant of graph geodesic convexity; proving a best possible transition for every missing-degree parameter distinguishes it from mere g-minimality recognition. The ensuing static/adaptive dimension pair is motivated by graph-convex online learning and provides a precise subfamily benchmark. No claim of novelty for general g-minimality is made.
